title: Executive Command Centre
objective: Provide a single cross-clinic overview of operational health, risk, workforce readiness, compliance, finance readiness and unresolved actions. The page should explain why a clinic is green, amber or red and allow the user to open the underlying record in one click.
primaryUsers: Owner / Director, Group Operations Manager, Senior Practice Manager, Finance and Quality Leads
tabs: Overview — Today’s priorities, all-location KPIs, urgent alerts and quick links.
My Day — Role-sensitive daily workspace for shifts, clocking, duties, tasks, training, handovers and alerts.
Clinic Health — Location cards with score, reasons, trend and drill-down.
KPI Scorecard — Comparable workforce, pay, quality, inventory, digital and risk measures.
Risk & Exceptions — Cross-module red/amber items ranked by severity and due date.
Reports — Saved management packs, period comparisons and exported summaries.
visuals: KPI strip for overdue actions, roster gaps, pay readiness, incidents, checklist completion and expiring evidence.
Clinic health cards with green/amber/red status plus plain-language reasons.
Top Risks table showing severity, owner, clinic, due date and days overdue.
Trend charts with comparison period selector and direct links to the relevant module.
Role-sensitive quick actions so users do not see actions they cannot perform.
rules: Every KPI must have a documented definition, owner and threshold.
A red/amber status must show the contributing records rather than an unexplained score.
Clinic comparisons should be normalised where size or activity volume materially changes interpretation.
Closed or archived items remain available in trend reports but do not appear in the active attention queue.
Users see only clinics and sensitive indicators allowed by their role.

flows.title: Morning executive review
steps: User opens the platform and lands on Overview with All Clinics or their default clinic selected.
The KPI strip loads current red and amber indicators; the user selects a card such as “Doctor pay blocked”.
A filtered detail drawer opens showing affected clinic, pay period, blocker, owner and due date.
The user clicks Open Source Record and is taken to the relevant module and exact item.
After the item is resolved, the dashboard status updates and the activity remains in history.

flows.title: Compare clinic performance
steps: User opens Clinic Health and selects the comparison period.
The page displays clinic cards ordered by risk or score.
User selects two or more clinics and clicks Compare.
A comparison view shows KPI definitions, current value, trend, threshold and underlying exceptions.
User clicks Create Management Action on a weak area, assigns an owner and due date, and the action appears in Action Inbox.

flows.title: Produce management pack
steps: User opens Reports and chooses Monthly Operations Pack.
A preview shows included clinics, period, KPI sections, unresolved risks and commentary fields.
User adds management commentary and excludes any section they are not authorised to share.
User clicks Generate Report, reviews the final preview and exports the approved pack.
The generated report is stored in report history with creator, date and filters.

flows.title: Role-Based My Day User Journey
flows.objective: Give reception, nursing, general staff, doctors and managers a simple daily starting point instead of requiring every user to interpret the executive dashboard.
flows.placement: Module 1 - Executive Command Centre, using a role-sensitive My Day tab.
steps: User signs in and lands on My Day for the default clinic and current date.
The page displays today's shift, clocking status, opening/closing duty, checklists, tasks, training and alerts.
The user selects the next required action, such as Clock In, Start Opening Checklist or View Shift.
Completed items leave the urgent area and remain visible in the daily timeline.
Unfinished items are included in the next handover or manager exception queue.
The user may switch clinic or date only where access permits.
rules: My Day is role and clinic sensitive.
Critical actions remain above the fold.
Patient records and appointment workflows are not displayed.

outputs: Measure: percentage of red/amber items resolved within target
Measure: number of unexplained or ownerless exceptions (target zero)

title: Action Inbox & Notification Centre
objective: Prevent important work from being lost in separate module screens or email. Every approval, failed check, overdue action, pay blocker, document review and high-risk alert should enter an owned queue with clear context and next steps.
primaryUsers: All users for personal actions, Practice Managers, Operations Managers, Approvers, Owners
tabs: My Actions — Items assigned directly to the logged-in user.
Team Queue — Items owned by the user’s team or clinic.
Approvals — Submitted records awaiting a decision.
Exceptions — Blocked, failed, skipped, overdue or mismatched records.
Escalations — High-risk or overdue items requiring elevated attention.
Completed — Recently completed decisions and actions with filters.
Delegations — Temporary approval cover, acting authority, effective dates and post-delegation review.
visuals: Queue cards with source module icon, clinic, status, owner, due date and risk.
Split-view mode: queue on the left and record preview/action panel on the right.
Reason modal for reject, override, snooze or reassignment actions.
Unread notification badge and notification preference controls.
Saved filters such as “Due today”, “My clinics”, “Pay blockers” and “High risk”.
rules: Action Inbox is the common approval entry point; duplicate standalone approval navigation should not be created.
Approvals must show the information needed to decide and a link to full evidence.
Reject, override, reassign and snooze actions require a reason.
The same item should not create multiple indistinguishable inbox entries for one user.
Escalation follows severity, due date and business ownership rules defined by the source module.

flows.title: Review and approve an item
steps: User opens Approvals and filters by clinic or module.
User selects an item; the right panel displays summary, evidence, prior comments and decision impact.
User clicks Approve or Request Changes.
A confirmation modal shows any downstream effect, such as publishing a roster or moving a pay run forward.
The decision is saved, the source record changes status and affected users receive notification.

flows.title: Resolve an exception
steps: User opens Exceptions and selects an attendance or checklist exception.
The panel shows the exception reason, affected workflow and blocking consequence.
User chooses Resolve, Reassign or Open Source depending on authority.
If an override is used, the user enters a mandatory reason and confirms the risk.
The item leaves the active queue only when the source record is no longer blocked.

flows.title: Escalate overdue work
steps: A manager opens Team Queue and sorts by days overdue.
The manager selects one or more items and clicks Escalate.
The escalation modal requires escalation owner, reason, new due date and notification recipients.
The items move to Escalations and display the escalation level.
When resolved, the history records original owner, escalation and final outcome.

flows.title: Approval Delegation and Absence Cover
flows.objective: Prevent pay, roster, compliance and operational approvals from becoming blocked while an authorised approver is absent.
flows.placement: Module 2 - Action Inbox & Notification Centre, supported by Module 3 permissions.
steps: Approver opens Delegations and clicks Create Delegation.
The approver selects the delegate, relevant modules, clinics, authority level and start/end dates.
A preview lists approvals and queues that will redirect.
Higher-risk or broad delegations are submitted for owner approval.
During the active period, the delegate sees eligible actions labelled Acting on behalf of.
The delegation ends automatically or may be ended early with a reason.
A post-delegation report shows all decisions taken, unresolved items and any exceptions.
rules: Delegation cannot exceed the delegator's own authority.
Sensitive modules may require separate approval.
Delegated decisions retain both the decision maker and original authority owner.

outputs: Measure: actions without an owner (target zero)
Measure: approval turnaround by module and clinic

title: Organisation, Locations, Users & Permissions
objective: Maintain the organisation structure and enforce location-aware, role-aware access across the platform. Clinic profiles, users, responsibilities, operating settings and historical access decisions are managed here.
primaryUsers: Owner / Director, Group Administrator, Operations Manager, Authorised Practice Manager, Auditor
tabs: Organisation — Group identity, business units and central contacts.
Clinics — Location profiles, hours, public holiday region and responsible managers.
Rooms & Areas — Operational areas used by rosters, assets, checklists and tickets.
Users — User accounts, status, assigned roles and clinic access.
Roles & Permissions — Role templates and permitted view/create/approve/export actions.
Business Settings — Pay periods, alert thresholds, review cycles and notification rules.
Access Reviews — Scheduled review of active permissions.
Audit History — Sensitive activity and access decision history.
Account Activation & Recovery — Invitation status, first-time access, lockout, reset and administrator-assisted recovery.
Clinic Lifecycle — New clinic opening, relocation, temporary closure, merger, service transfer, permanent closure and reopening.
visuals: Clinic cards with status, responsible manager, hours and unresolved setup gaps.
User access matrix showing modules against view/create/approve/export permissions.
Role assignment drawer with clinic scope and effective dates.
Access review wizard listing stale, excessive or unused permissions.
Audit timeline filtered by user, clinic, module, action and date.
rules: A user may work across multiple clinics but only approved locations appear in their switcher.
Sensitive modules require explicit permission; general clinic access alone is insufficient.
Inactive users and clinics remain in history but cannot be selected for new work.
No shared generic login should be used for sensitive activities.
Changes to roles, permissions, settings and clinic responsibility are auditable and effective-dated.

flows.title: Add a clinic
steps: Administrator opens Clinics and clicks Add Clinic.
A stepper opens for Identity, Contact, Hours, Rooms, Responsibilities and Alerts.
Administrator assigns responsible manager, nurse and escalation contacts.
A review screen highlights missing mandatory information.
Administrator clicks Activate Clinic; the clinic becomes selectable in approved modules.

flows.title: Onboard a user
steps: Administrator opens Users and clicks Invite User.
The form captures identity, contact, user type and employment relationship.
Administrator selects one or more clinics and assigns a role template.
A permission preview shows what the user can view and change.
Administrator confirms the invitation; the user remains Pending until activation requirements are met.

flows.title: Suspend and offboard access
steps: Manager opens a user profile and clicks Suspend or Start Offboarding.
A modal asks for effective date, reason and whether temporary or permanent.
The system displays impacted shifts, tasks, approvals, remote access and sensitive permissions.
Manager reassigns owned work and confirms access removal checklist.
The user is prevented from new activity while historical records remain visible.

flows.title: Conduct access review
steps: Authorised reviewer opens Access Reviews and selects clinic and review period.
The page lists active users, last activity, roles, sensitive permissions and exceptions.
Reviewer confirms, changes or removes each questionable permission.
Reviewer adds an overall sign-off comment and completes the review.
A review report is stored and unresolved changes enter Action Inbox.

flows.title: First-Time Access, Sign-In Recovery and Account Lockout
flows.objective: Provide a complete journey from invitation to safe platform entry and a controlled path for forgotten credentials or locked accounts.
flows.placement: Module 3 - Organisation, Locations, Users & Permissions; Account Activation & Recovery workspace.
steps: Invited user opens the invitation and confirms identity.
User creates sign-in details and completes required security setup.
A preview shows assigned clinics, role and permitted modules.
User accepts required privacy, security and acceptable-use acknowledgements.
User completes any mandatory profile setup and enters a guided first-use tour.
If access fails later, the user selects Reset Password, Unlock Account or Contact Administrator.
Sensitive recovery requests enter the administrator queue and are closed only after identity and authority are confirmed.
rules: Invitation and recovery links have an expiry.
No user receives broader access through recovery than already approved.
All administrator-assisted recovery is auditable.

flows.title: Approval Delegation and Absence Cover
flows.objective: Prevent pay, roster, compliance and operational approvals from becoming blocked while an authorised approver is absent.
flows.placement: Module 2 - Action Inbox & Notification Centre, supported by Module 3 permissions.
steps: Approver opens Delegations and clicks Create Delegation.
The approver selects the delegate, relevant modules, clinics, authority level and start/end dates.
A preview lists approvals and queues that will redirect.
Higher-risk or broad delegations are submitted for owner approval.
During the active period, the delegate sees eligible actions labelled Acting on behalf of.
The delegation ends automatically or may be ended early with a reason.
A post-delegation report shows all decisions taken, unresolved items and any exceptions.
rules: Delegation cannot exceed the delegator's own authority.
Sensitive modules may require separate approval.
Delegated decisions retain both the decision maker and original authority owner.

flows.title: Clinic Opening, Relocation, Temporary Closure and Permanent Closure
flows.objective: Control the full lifecycle of a medical-centre location and ensure no workforce, asset, supplier, communication or governance responsibility is overlooked.
flows.placement: Module 3 - Clinic Lifecycle, linked to Modules 13, 15, 16, 17 and 19.
steps: Authorised user selects Start Clinic Transition and chooses the transition type.

The guided impact assessment identifies affected staff, doctors, future rosters, assets, stock, suppliers, phone/website services, policies, accreditation evidence, tickets, incidents and pay responsibilities.
Actions, owners and due dates are assigned for each affected area.
Communications are drafted, reviewed and approved for relevant audiences.
Staff, doctors, assets, stock, contracts and open responsibilities are transferred, suspended or closed.
The readiness dashboard is reviewed and unresolved blockers are escalated.
Final approver confirms the effective date and changes the clinic status.
Historical records remain available under the former location and the transition receives a post-change review.
rules: A clinic cannot close while critical responsibilities remain ownerless.
Historical records are never moved in a way that obscures the original clinic.
Patient transfer and appointment actions remain in the clinical/practice system.

flows.title: Workforce Data Access and Correction Request
flows.objective: Allow staff and doctors to request access to, or correction of, permitted business records about themselves.
flows.placement: Modules 3, 4 and 13, through a controlled self-service request.
steps: User opens self-service and submits an access or correction request.
The request identifies the record/category and explains the requested correction where applicable.
Authorised owner reviews identity, scope, sensitivity and any linked legal/retention restriction.
For access, permitted information is prepared and restricted third-party or sensitive information is excluded where appropriate.
For correction, the source owner approves, rejects or requests evidence.
Approved correction updates the source record through normal version/history rules.
The user receives the outcome, reason and completion date.
The request closes with a retained response history.
rules: Self-service access does not grant general HR, finance or incident permissions.
Corrections do not erase valid historical facts.
Response time and escalation follow approved privacy/business rules.
Priority 3 - Future Service Maturity

outputs: Measure: inactive users retaining active access (target zero)

title: Staff & Doctor Management
objective: Maintain complete and effective-dated business profiles for non-doctor staff and doctors. The module supplies approved workforce information to roster, attendance, staff pay, doctor pay, training, credentials and access lifecycle workflows.
primaryUsers: HR / Payroll, Practice Managers, Owners, Staff self-service users, Doctors
tabs: Staff Directory — Reception, nursing, management, administration, contractors and other staff.
Doctor Directory — Doctor business profile, locations, contract and payment settings.
HR Documents — Contracts, identity, certificates, performance and employment records.
Leave / Away Days — Requests, approvals, balances or reference status, coverage notes and calendar.
Award Rules — Classification, employment type, pay category mapping and effective dates.
Provider Credentials — AHPRA and role-specific credential evidence, expiry and review.
Onboarding — Readiness checklist, induction and access setup.
Offboarding — Work reassignment, document closure and access removal.
Employment Changes — Transfer, promotion, role, manager, employment type and clinic reassignment with effective dates.
Return to Work & Restrictions — Leave amendments, cancellations, return confirmation and controlled duty restrictions.
visuals: Profile header with readiness score, employment/contract status, default clinic and critical expiry badges.
Add Staff / Add Doctor multi-step wizard: Basic, Contact, Emergency, Employment/Contract, Locations, Pay Profile, Documents, Preferences and Review.
Effective-dated history for rates, classifications, contract terms, GST status and bank detail changes.
Document expiry calendar and missing-document checklist by role.
Onboarding/offboarding progress panel with owner and due date for each action.
rules: A person cannot become Active for roster or pay until mandatory fields are complete or an authorised temporary exception is recorded.
Pay and contract settings are never overwritten; changes create a new effective-dated version.
Mandatory documents differ by role and clinic responsibility.
Leave and away days must feed roster warnings and coverage planning.
Suspension or termination triggers reassignment and access-removal actions.
Sensitive HR, bank and contract information is restricted to authorised roles.

flows.title: Add a staff member
steps: HR user opens Staff Directory and clicks Add Staff.
The wizard opens at Basic Details; the user enters name, contact, emergency contact and preferred communication.
Employment & Locations captures role, employment type, default clinic, additional clinics, start date and manager.
Award & Pay Profile captures approved classification mapping without duplicating payroll calculations.
Documents & Readiness shows required uploads and training; the profile can be saved as Draft.
Reviewer clicks Activate once mandatory items are complete; the person becomes selectable for permitted rosters and tasks.

flows.title: Add a doctor
steps: Authorised user opens Doctor Directory and clicks Add Doctor.
The wizard captures business identity, ABN/GST status, contact, payment email and clinic assignments.
Contract & Payment captures percentage or agreed rule, effective date, payment cycle and bank details with restricted visibility.
Credentials captures required evidence and expiry dates.
A review screen shows Doctor Pay and BBPIP readiness.
Approver activates the profile; future transactions use the effective contract rule.

flows.title: Request and approve leave
steps: Staff member opens Leave / Away Days and clicks Request Leave.
The form captures dates, type, notes and attachment where required.
A coverage preview shows rostered shifts and potential gaps.
Manager receives an Action Inbox approval and approves, rejects or requests changes.
Approved leave updates the calendar and triggers roster warnings for affected planning periods.

flows.title: Renew an expiring document
steps: The expiry dashboard flags an approaching certificate or credential.
Owner clicks Send Reminder or opens the person’s document panel.
Staff/doctor uploads replacement evidence and submits it for review.
Reviewer verifies dates and status, then approves or rejects with reason.
The new version becomes Current; the prior version remains in history.

flows.title: Offboard a worker
steps: Manager clicks Start Offboarding from the profile.
The checklist identifies future shifts, open tasks, approvals, training, assets, remote access and sensitive permissions.
Owners are assigned for reassignment, asset return and document completion.
Access is suspended on the effective date and open work is reassigned.
Reviewer signs off the checklist and the profile becomes Archived while history remains reportable.

flows.title: Leave Amendment, Cancellation and Return to Work
flows.objective: Manage changes after leave approval and safely return staff to normal duties where confirmation or restrictions are required.
flows.placement: Module 4 - Staff & Doctor Management; Leave / Away Days and Return to Work workspaces.
steps: Staff member opens approved leave and selects Amend or Cancel.
The page displays affected rosters, duties and pay periods.
The staff member enters the requested change and submits it.
Manager approves, rejects or requests changes after reviewing coverage and payroll impact.
Approved changes update the leave calendar and create roster/pay warnings where required.
On return, the staff member or manager completes Return to Work confirmation where applicable.
Any temporary restrictions or follow-up actions are recorded with controlled visibility and an end/review date.
rules: Approved leave is not silently edited.
Restrictions are visible only to roles that need them for safe duty assignment.
Payroll and roster source records retain the effective dates of every change.

flows.title: Worker Transfer, Promotion and Employment Change
flows.objective: Control effective-dated changes to a worker's role, manager, employment type, classification or clinic assignment.
flows.placement: Module 4 - Employment Changes.
steps: HR opens the worker profile and clicks Start Employment Change.
User selects transfer, promotion, role change, manager change, employment-type change or clinic reassignment.
The impact panel identifies permissions, roster, training, award/pay and work-ownership consequences.
Required new documents, training and approvals are assigned.
Approvers review the before-and-after summary and effective date.
On approval, the new arrangement becomes active on the effective date.
Previous arrangements remain visible in history and affected users receive notifications.
rules: The current arrangement remains active until the approved effective date.
Pay and classification changes create new versions rather than overwriting history.
Access should reduce or expand only according to approved role and clinic scope.

flows.title: Credential Expiry, Suspension and Reactivation
flows.objective: Define the operational response when mandatory credentials expire or become invalid.
flows.placement: Module 4 - Provider Credentials and Onboarding/Readiness.
steps: Reminder actions are issued before expiry according to the credential rule.
If the credential expires, the profile changes to Not Ready or Restricted for affected duties.
The manager reviews future rosters, checklists and responsibilities impacted by the expiry.
Manager removes/reassigns affected work, suspends eligibility or records an authorised temporary exception.
The worker uploads updated evidence and submits it for verification.
Reviewer approves or rejects the renewal.
On approval, the credential becomes Current and eligible duties are reactivated from the approved date.
rules: Expired mandatory evidence cannot be treated as current.
Any temporary exception requires owner, reason, expiry and risk acknowledgement.
Reactivation is limited to the duties supported by the approved evidence.

flows.title: Doctor Bank Detail Change and Verification
flows.objective: Protect doctor payments from unauthorised or incorrectly entered bank-detail changes.
flows.placement: Module 4 doctor profile and Module 8 Doctor Pay Command Centre.
steps: Doctor or authorised finance user clicks Request Bank Detail Change.
New details are entered and remain Pending Verification; approved current details remain active.
The approved verification procedure is completed and evidence/reference is recorded.
Where required, a second authorised approver confirms or rejects the change.
The effective date is set and the doctor receives confirmation through the approved channel.
Doctor Pay displays a warning for pay runs affected by the change date.
Previous details remain restricted in effective-dated history.
rules: Bank details are never changed through an unverified email instruction alone.
The requester cannot complete all approval steps where separation of duties is required.
Only approved effective details are used for manual payment preparation.

flows.title: Workforce Data Access and Correction Request
flows.objective: Allow staff and doctors to request access to, or correction of, permitted business records about themselves.
flows.placement: Modules 3, 4 and 13, through a controlled self-service request.
steps: User opens self-service and submits an access or correction request.
The request identifies the record/category and explains the requested correction where applicable.
Authorised owner reviews identity, scope, sensitivity and any linked legal/retention restriction.
For access, permitted information is prepared and restricted third-party or sensitive information is excluded where appropriate.
For correction, the source owner approves, rejects or requests evidence.
Approved correction updates the source record through normal version/history rules.
The user receives the outcome, reason and completion date.
The request closes with a retained response history.
rules: Self-service access does not grant general HR, finance or incident permissions.
Corrections do not erase valid historical facts.
Response time and escalation follow approved privacy/business rules.
Priority 3 - Future Service Maturity

title: Roster & Shift Management
objective: Plan and publish staffing coverage across clinics while preventing cross-location conflicts, leave clashes, missing role coverage, avoidable overtime and unclear opening/closing responsibilities.
primaryUsers: Practice Managers, Operations Managers, Reception and Nursing Leads, Staff self-service users
tabs: Week View — Primary drag-and-drop roster by clinic, role or staff member.
Coverage — Heat map of staffing and role gaps by time of day.
Availability — Normal patterns, exceptions, leave and away days.
Shift Requests — Swap, release and change requests awaiting review.
Open Shifts — Unfilled and urgent shifts offered to eligible staff across one or more clinics.
Published History — Versions, change reasons and notification status.
Roster Reports — Hours forecast, duties, conflicts and publication history.
visuals: Dense weekly grid with clinic, role and staff views.
Coverage heat map and warning banner for gaps, double bookings, leave and excessive hours.
Shift card badges for opening, closing, role duty, break and status.
Pre-publication validation drawer listing blocking and warning items.
Duty impact preview during shift change.
rules: Cross-location double booking must be blocked or require authorised override with reason.
Published roster changes record who, what, why, when and who was notified.
Opening, closing and role-specific checklist ownership follows the approved shift holder.
Leave, availability, training readiness and inactive status influence eligible staff selection.
Roster forecasts show hours by week, pay period, staff and clinic before publication.

flows.title: Build and publish roster
steps: Manager opens Week View and selects clinic, week and role view.
Manager copies a prior week or starts from a template.
Shifts are added or adjusted and staff are assigned from an eligibility list.
Manager clicks Validate Roster; blocking issues and warnings appear in a drawer.
Manager resolves gaps or records authorised overrides.
Manager clicks Publish, confirms notification recipients and the roster becomes visible to staff.

flows.title: Staff shift-swap request
steps: Staff member opens My Roster, selects a shift and clicks Request Swap / Release.
The request drawer shows eligible replacement staff and the duties that will transfer.
Staff member selects a proposed replacement, adds reason and submits.
Replacement acceptance is captured where required, then the manager reviews warnings and impact.
On approval, the published roster changes, duties transfer and affected users are notified.

flows.title: Emergency roster change
steps: Manager clicks Emergency Change on the affected shift.
The modal requires emergency reason, replacement, timing and approver.
The page shows conflicts, hours and duty impact but permits an authorised override.
Manager confirms; notifications are sent immediately.
The change is tagged Emergency and appears in the stability report and audit history.

flows.title: Open Shift and Urgent Coverage Broadcast
flows.objective: Fill planned or sudden roster gaps quickly while preserving eligibility, fatigue, leave, training and cross-clinic controls.
flows.placement: Module 5 - Roster & Shift Management; Open Shifts tab.
steps: Manager selects an uncovered shift and clicks Create Open Shift.
Eligible staff are filtered using role, clinic access, availability, leave, training status, current hours and conflicts.
Manager selects the offer audience and response deadline.
Eligible staff receive the offer and choose Accept or Decline.
If multiple staff accept, the manager reviews suitability and selects the final assignment.
Roster validation checks conflicts, hours and transferred duties.
The manager confirms the assignment; the roster and opening/closing responsibilities update and all affected users are notified.
rules: Acceptance is provisional until the manager confirms where multiple users respond.
An urgent override requires a reason.
The flow does not expose restricted HR or pay information to other staff.

outputs: Shift change and emergency change register
Measure: unresolved coverage gaps at publication

title: Time & Attendance
objective: Record actual work time against rostered shifts, manage breaks and missed punches, and create approved timesheets without confusing attendance records with checklist completion.
primaryUsers: All rostered staff, Practice Managers, Operations Managers, Payroll Users
tabs: Live Attendance — Who is expected, clocked in, late, on break or missing.
My Clock — Staff clock-in/out and break actions.
Exceptions — Missing, late, early, location, break and overtime exceptions.
Timesheets — Pay-period view of actual hours and approvals.
Approval History — Corrections, reasons, approvers and lock history.
Reports — Attendance variance and exception trends.
visuals: Large clock action card showing current shift, clinic and next expected action.
Live attendance board with clear non-colour status labels.
Exception queue ordered by payroll impact and due date.
Rostered versus actual timeline for each shift.
Timesheet summary with regular, overtime, leave and unresolved hours.
rules: Clocking should link to a rostered shift wherever possible.
Attendance exceptions must not automatically deny payment for time that may have been worked.
Manual corrections require reason and manager approval.
Timesheets cannot be finalised with unresolved blocking exceptions unless an authorised override is recorded.
Checklists and attendance remain separate records even when accessed from the same shift screen.

flows.title: Normal clock-in/out
steps: Staff member opens My Clock and sees the current rostered shift.
Staff clicks Clock In; the screen confirms clinic, shift and timestamp.
During the shift, Start Break and End Break update the live status.
At completion, staff clicks Clock Out and reviews the shift summary.
A clean shift moves automatically to the manager’s timesheet review without an exception.

flows.title: Missed punch correction
steps: Staff member clicks Report Missed Punch and selects the affected shift.
The form captures missing event, proposed time, reason and optional evidence.
Manager receives an exception item and compares roster, recorded events and note.
Manager approves, adjusts or rejects the proposed correction with reason.
The timesheet recalculates and the decision is retained in Approval History.

flows.title: Pay-period attendance approval
steps: Manager opens Timesheets for the pay period and filters to Unresolved.
The screen groups clean timesheets and exception-affected timesheets.
Manager bulk-approves clean records, then opens each exception for decision.
When all blockers are resolved, manager clicks Approve Period.
Payroll users see the location as Ready in Staff Pay.

outputs: Measure: repeated missed punches by clinic/person

title: Staff Pay & Payroll Preparation
objective: Convert approved attendance, leave and authorised pay categories into payroll-ready information, support review and export to Xero or the selected payroll process, and retain reconciliation history without replacing the payroll/accounting system.
primaryUsers: Payroll / Finance, Practice Managers, Operations Managers, Owners
tabs: Pay Run — Staff and clinic readiness for the selected pay period.
Exceptions — Attendance, leave, classification and category blockers.
Variances — Roster-to-actual and prior-period differences.
Leave & Allowances — Approved leave, public holiday and authorised allowance review.
Export & Reconciliation — Approved output, export record and confirmation.
History — Locked periods, corrections and re-open decisions.
Corrections & Final Pay — Export rejection, final pay, overpayment, underpayment and replacement export control.
visuals: Pay-run control tower showing Ready, Blocked, In Review, Exported, Reconciled and Locked by clinic.
Variance flags for unusual overtime, missing leave, category changes and large roster differences.
Staff-level pay summary with source attendance and approval links.
Final review checklist before export.
Export history with creator, date, period, status and reconciliation note.
rules: Only approved attendance and approved leave enter a payroll-ready run.
Rates and classifications come from effective-dated Staff Management settings and require payroll validation.
A pay run with unresolved blockers cannot be marked Ready without an authorised override.
Exporting does not mean payroll has been paid; reconciliation status is recorded separately.
Reopening a locked period requires elevated approval and a reason.

flows.title: Prepare a pay run
steps: Payroll user selects the pay period and clicks Create Pay Run.
The module loads approved attendance, leave and current classification mappings.
The control tower identifies clinics and staff that are Ready or Blocked.
Payroll user resolves exceptions through the linked source records.
Once clear, payroll user clicks Recalculate and reviews totals and variances.
Each clinic is approved and the full run moves to Final Review.

flows.title: Export and reconcile
steps: Authorised user opens Export & Reconciliation and reviews the final checklist.
User clicks Export to Xero and confirms included employees and period.
The generated output is recorded with version and totals.
After payroll processing outside the platform, the user returns and records reconciliation result and notes.
The period is marked Reconciled and Locked.

flows.title: Correct a prior period
steps: Payroll user opens History and selects a locked period.
User clicks Reopen with Approval and enters reason and affected staff.
An elevated approver reviews the financial and reporting impact.
On approval, only authorised corrections can be made and a new version is created.
The corrected output is re-exported and both versions remain in history.

flows.title: Payroll Export Rejection, Final Pay and Overpayment Correction
flows.objective: Cover common payroll exceptions that occur after standard pay preparation.
flows.placement: Module 7 - Staff Pay & Payroll Preparation; Corrections & Final Pay.
steps: For export rejection, payroll opens the failed output, reviews employee-level errors, corrects the source records and generates a replacement export version.
For final pay, offboarding creates a final-pay action covering approved hours, leave, allowances and outstanding corrections.
Payroll reviews and approves final-pay inputs, exports the result and records reconciliation.
For overpayment or underpayment, payroll records the variance, affected period, likely cause and communication requirement.
The correction method and approval are recorded.
The adjustment is processed in the appropriate pay period or external process.
The original, replacement and correction records remain linked in history.
rules: A replacement export does not erase the rejected version.
Final pay must be completed before workforce offboarding is fully closed where applicable.
Recovery or correction actions require authorised review and clear communication history.

outputs: Staff pay review and variance report
Measure: pay runs completed by cut-off

title: Doctor Pay Command Centre
objective: Manage doctor payment calculations from approved Best Practice/practice-system activity through contract rules, adjustments, reconciliation, approval, payslip generation, email delivery, storage, doctor portal publication and confirmation of the manual bank transfer.
primaryUsers: Finance / Payroll, Owner / Director, Authorised Practice Manager, Doctors, Auditors
tabs: Pay Run — Current cycle, doctors, locations, totals and status.
Transactions — Imported activity matched to doctor and location.
Contract Rules — Effective percentage, fixed rules, GST and approved exceptions.
Adjustments — Authorised additions, deductions and corrections.
Reconciliation — Source totals, excluded items, prior adjustments and variance.
Approvals — Finance and owner decision queue.
Payslips — Generated, approved, reissued and archived statements.
Email Log — Delivery, failure, resend and recipient history.
Manual Payments — Bank transfer date, reference, amount and confirmer.
Doctor Portal — Doctor-visible payslips, statements and payment status.
Queries & Disputes — Doctor-submitted pay queries, evidence, finance response and resolution history.
Payment Exceptions — Failed, returned, partial and replacement manual payment records.
visuals: Pay-run progress stepper: Imported → Calculated → Reconciled → Approved → Payslips Sent → Manual Payment Recorded → Locked.
Doctor summary cards showing gross activity, exclusions, adjustments, rate, GST and amount payable.
Unmatched transaction queue and reconciliation variance panel.
Payslip preview with email delivery status and stored version.
Manual payment register with separate status from payslip delivery.
rules: Doctor contract rules and GST settings are effective-dated and sourced from the approved doctor profile.
Unmatched, duplicate or excluded transactions must be resolved or explicitly approved before finalisation.
Adjustments require type, amount, reason, evidence, creator and approver.
Payslips are generated only from the approved reconciled version.
Email failure does not reverse approval; it creates a resend action.
Marking paid requires manual transfer date, amount, payment reference and authorised confirmer.
Corrections and reissues create a new version and never erase the original.

flows.title: Full doctor pay run
steps: Finance user opens Pay Run, selects the payment cycle and clicks Import / Refresh Transactions.
Transactions are matched to doctor and clinic; unmatched items appear in a blocking queue.
User resolves unmatched items and clicks Calculate Pay Run.
The platform applies the effective contract rule, GST treatment and approved adjustments.
User opens Reconciliation, compares source totals, exclusions and calculated payable amounts, and resolves variances.
User clicks Submit for Approval; the authorised approver reviews summary and doctor-level detail.
After approval, user clicks Generate Payslips, previews them and confirms Email Payslips and Publish to Portal.
An authorised user completes the bank transfer outside the platform.
The user returns to Manual Payments, records transfer details and clicks Mark Completed.
When every doctor is resolved, the pay run is Locked.

flows.title: Add an adjustment
steps: User opens a doctor in Adjustments and clicks Add Adjustment.
A modal captures category, amount, GST treatment if relevant, reason, evidence and effective pay run.
The adjustment enters Pending Approval and recalculates the provisional amount.
Approver reviews the adjustment in Action Inbox and approves or rejects it.
Approved adjustment appears on the reconciliation and payslip with a clear label.

flows.title: Reissue a payslip
steps: Finance user opens Payslips and selects the original document.
User clicks Reissue and chooses correction, recipient update or delivery retry.
For a financial correction, the pay run must be reopened through the authorised correction workflow.
A new version is generated with reissue reason and reference to the original.
The new payslip is emailed/published and the email log records the outcome.

flows.title: Doctor self-service review
steps: Doctor opens Doctor Portal and sees recent pay cycles and status.
Doctor selects a cycle to view payslip, transaction schedule and payment status.
Doctor clicks Raise Query if clarification is needed and enters a category and message.
The query creates a finance action linked to the exact pay run and doctor.
Finance responds and the query history remains visible to the doctor.

flows.title: Doctor Bank Detail Change and Verification
flows.objective: Protect doctor payments from unauthorised or incorrectly entered bank-detail changes.
flows.placement: Module 4 doctor profile and Module 8 Doctor Pay Command Centre.
steps: Doctor or authorised finance user clicks Request Bank Detail Change.
New details are entered and remain Pending Verification; approved current details remain active.
The approved verification procedure is completed and evidence/reference is recorded.
Where required, a second authorised approver confirms or rejects the change.
The effective date is set and the doctor receives confirmation through the approved channel.
Doctor Pay displays a warning for pay runs affected by the change date.
Previous details remain restricted in effective-dated history.
rules: Bank details are never changed through an unverified email instruction alone.
The requester cannot complete all approval steps where separation of duties is required.
Only approved effective details are used for manual payment preparation.

flows.title: Doctor Pay Dispute, Failed Transfer and Partial Payment
flows.objective: Provide a controlled resolution path for doctor queries and manual payment exceptions.
flows.placement: Module 8 - Queries & Disputes and Payment Exceptions.
steps: Doctor selects a payslip or transaction and clicks Raise Pay Query.
Doctor chooses a category such as missing activity, calculation issue, adjustment dispute, GST issue or payment not received.
Finance accepts the query, reviews linked source information and requests further information where needed.
If a financial correction is required, the authorised pay-run reopening and reissue process is followed.
If a transfer failed or was returned, finance records the payment exception and verifies approved bank details.
For partial payment, the paid amount is recorded and the remaining balance stays open.
Replacement payment details are recorded after the manual transfer is completed.
Finance sends the outcome to the doctor and closes the dispute only after resolution is confirmed.
rules: A query does not alter approved pay automatically.
All financial corrections create a new version.
Payment status, payslip delivery and dispute status remain separate but linked.

outputs: Measure: pay runs completed by payment date
Measure: unmatched or disputed items at approval

title: BBPIP Forecast & Reconciliation
objective: Provide an operational workspace for Bulk Billing Practice Incentive Program forecasting, doctor/location contribution review, evidence readiness, variance analysis and final reconciliation using approved practice-system summaries.
primaryUsers: Owner / Director, Finance, Practice Managers, Doctors with approved visibility, Compliance Reviewers
tabs: Forecast — Current quarter/period estimate and trend.
Doctor / Clinic Contribution — Contribution summaries with filters.
Eligibility & Rules — Business interpretation, required evidence and effective dates.
Compliance Gaps — Missing or inconsistent evidence and exceptions.
Reconciliation — Forecast versus actual result and variance reasons.
Evidence — Linked reports, approvals and supporting files.
History — Prior forecasts, versions and final outcomes.
visuals: Forecast KPI cards for estimated amount, trend, confidence, unresolved gaps and period end.
Doctor/clinic contribution table with drill-down to approved summary data.
Compliance gap queue with owner, due date and potential impact.
Waterfall or variance view from forecast to actual result.
Period timeline showing forecast versions, reviews and final reconciliation.
rules: Forecasts are estimates and must be labelled clearly until final reconciliation.
Business rules and eligibility assumptions require owner, effective date and review date.
Missing evidence or data-quality issues reduce forecast confidence and create owned actions.
Final actual outcomes are recorded separately from forecast versions.
Reconciliation variance requires a reason category and commentary.

flows.title: Create a forecast
steps: User opens Forecast, selects period and clicks Refresh Approved Data.
The module displays source completeness and any blocking gaps.
User resolves or assigns gaps, then clicks Run Forecast.
The estimate displays by clinic and doctor with assumptions and confidence level.
User submits the estimate for review and the approver confirms or requests changes.
Approved forecast becomes the current management baseline.

flows.title: Resolve a compliance gap
steps: User opens Compliance Gaps and selects an item.
The panel explains the missing evidence, affected period and estimated impact.
User assigns an owner and due date or links existing evidence.
Reviewer verifies the evidence and marks the gap Resolved or Not Applicable with reason.
Forecast confidence and affected totals update after the next refresh.

flows.title: Reconcile actual outcome
steps: Finance user opens Reconciliation and enters or imports the approved actual result.
The module compares actual result to the latest approved forecast.
User categorises each material variance and adds supporting notes/evidence.
Approver reviews the reconciliation and clicks Finalise Period.
The period is locked and appears in history with forecast accuracy metrics.

outputs: Measure: unresolved high-impact gaps before period end

title: Tasks, Checklists, Meetings & Actions
objective: Combine personal tasks, operational checklists, opening/closing duties, manager reviews, meeting minutes and follow-up actions so no duty or decision remains unowned.
primaryUsers: All Staff, Practice Managers, Nursing Leads, Operations Managers, Quality / Accreditation Leads
tabs: My Tasks — Personal assigned work and due dates.
Team Tasks — Clinic/team tasks with ownership and status.
Active Checklists — Today’s recurring checklists by role and location.
Opening / Closing — Shift-linked duty checklists.
Manager Reviews — Daily, weekly, monthly and periodic review packs.
Template Builder — Create and version checklist templates.
Meetings — Meeting agenda, minutes and attendance.
Action Register — Actions created from meetings, incidents, audits and reviews.
Handover — End-of-shift and end-of-day transfer of unresolved operational matters with acknowledgement.
Reports — Completion, exceptions and overdue trends.
visuals: Today panel showing due tasks and active checklists before secondary lists.
Checklist item types: tick, yes/no, number, temperature, text, photo/file and sign-off.
Progress bar and exception badge for each active checklist.
Template creation stepper: Details → Frequency → Items → Assignment → Evidence → Review → Publish.
Meeting screen with agenda on left, live minutes and action capture on right.
rules: Checklists can be role-specific, location-specific, shift-specific and frequency-based.
Skipped or failed mandatory items require reason and may require evidence or escalation.
Opening/closing duties transfer automatically after an approved roster change.
Published templates are version-controlled; active checklist records retain the version used.
Meeting actions require owner and due date and automatically appear in Action Inbox.
A checklist exception can create a ticket, incident, stock action or document evidence without re-entering context.

flows.title: Build and publish a checklist
steps: Manager opens Template Builder and clicks Create Checklist Template.
The stepper captures name, purpose, location, role, frequency and active period.
Manager adds sections and item types, marks mandatory items and defines evidence for failed/skipped responses.
Assignment step previews which staff or shifts will receive the checklist.
Reviewer checks the template and clicks Publish.
The template becomes active at the next scheduled occurrence and prior versions remain in history.

flows.title: Complete opening checklist
steps: Rostered opening staff opens Opening / Closing from the shift card.
The active checklist shows ordered items and required evidence.
Staff completes items; a failed item prompts reason and displays Raise Ticket or Raise Incident.
Staff signs off and submits the checklist.
Manager sees completion status and any exception action in the review queue.

flows.title: Conduct a management meeting
steps: Chair opens Meetings and clicks Create Meeting.
Chair selects a template, clinic/group scope, attendees, agenda and linked reports.
During the meeting, decisions and notes are recorded; clicking Add Action captures owner, due date and linked module.
Chair reviews minutes and clicks Publish Minutes.
Open actions move to Action Register and automatically carry into the next meeting until closed.

flows.title: Close a task/action
steps: Owner opens My Tasks or Action Register and selects the item.
Owner adds outcome, evidence and any follow-up.
If approval is required, the item moves to manager review.
Approver confirms completion or reopens with reason.
Closed item remains searchable and included in completion reporting.

flows.title: Daily and Shift Handover
flows.objective: Create a formal transfer of unresolved operational matters between shifts, days and responsible managers.
flows.placement: Module 10 - Tasks, Checklists, Meetings & Actions; Handover tab.
steps: Outgoing user clicks Create Handover near the end of the shift or day.
The platform suggests unresolved operational items from linked modules.
User confirms relevant items and adds concise operational notes without unnecessary patient information.
Each item is assigned to the incoming person, role or manager.
Incoming user opens the handover and acknowledges receipt.
High-risk or unacknowledged items escalate according to due time and severity.
The handover closes when required items are acknowledged, while individual actions remain open until resolved.
rules: Acknowledgement does not equal completion.
High-risk items cannot be removed without a reason.
Handover history remains part of the clinic daily record.

flows.title: Missed Checklist, Retrospective Completion and Waiver
flows.objective: Handle an entire scheduled checklist occurrence that was not started or submitted on time.
flows.placement: Module 10 - Active Checklists and Exceptions.
steps: A scheduled checklist remains unstarted or incomplete after the due threshold.
The assigned user and manager receive an alert.
Manager reviews the operational context and selects Complete Late, Reassign, Mark Not Required or Record Operational Failure.
Late completion requires a reason and evidence where defined.
A waiver requires an authorised reason and does not appear as normal completion.
High-risk missed controls create an incident or management action.
The occurrence closes with its true outcome and appears correctly in compliance reporting.
rules: A missed occurrence cannot be backdated to appear on time.
Waiver and retrospective completion are permission controlled.
High-risk failures retain escalation history.

outputs: Measure: actions closed by due date

title: Training & Learning Management
objective: Assign, deliver and monitor mandatory and optional learning, policy acknowledgements, induction, assessments and competency evidence across staff, doctors, roles and clinics.
primaryUsers: Training Administrators, Practice Managers, Staff, Doctors, Quality Leads
tabs: Catalogue — Courses, policy acknowledgements and learning resources.
My Learning — Assigned, due, overdue and completed learning.
Assignments — Role, clinic and individual assignment rules.
Sessions — Scheduled face-to-face or live training.
Assessments — Questions, pass rules and reassessment.
Competencies — Observed competency and evidence.
Certificates & Expiry — Uploaded or generated certificates and renewal dates.
Exemptions & Prior Learning — Evidence-based exemption, recognition and expiry management.
Reports — Completion, overdue and readiness reporting.
visuals: Learning cards with due date, estimated duration, progress and status.
Course builder with content, assessment, acknowledgement and certificate settings.
Role readiness matrix showing mandatory training against people.
Expiry calendar and reminder timeline.
Manager view of overdue items affecting roster or responsibility readiness.
rules: Mandatory learning rules can be assigned by role, clinic, responsibility or policy version.
Training completion and policy acknowledgement are distinct where both are required.
Expired or missing mandatory training can create roster or duty warnings.
Extensions require reason, owner and revised due date.
Course and assessment versions are retained for historical evidence.

flows.title: Create and assign learning
steps: Training admin opens Catalogue and clicks Create Course.
The builder captures title, purpose, content, assessment, pass mark, validity period and certificate requirement.
Admin selects assignment rules by role, clinic or individual.
A preview lists affected people and due dates.
Admin publishes the course; assignments appear in My Learning and notifications are sent.

flows.title: Complete training
steps: User opens My Learning and selects an assigned course.
The course screen shows sections, progress and required assessment or acknowledgement.
User completes content and submits the assessment.
On pass, completion is recorded and a certificate is generated or upload requested.
If failed, the user receives feedback and a reassessment action according to the course rule.

flows.title: Record observed competency
steps: Manager opens Competencies and selects a person and competency.
The form displays the observation checklist and required evidence.
Manager records outcome, date, notes and next review date.
If competent, readiness updates; if not yet competent, remedial training/action is assigned.
The competency remains available in the person’s training history.

flows.title: Training Exemption, Prior Learning and Role-Change Reassignment
flows.objective: Recognise valid existing competence and recalculate learning requirements when roles or clinics change.
flows.placement: Module 11 - Exemptions & Prior Learning and Assignments.
steps: User or manager opens the training requirement and clicks Request Exemption / Prior Learning.
Evidence, issuing body, completion date and validity period are submitted.
Training administrator reviews the evidence and approves, rejects or requests more information.
Approved exemption satisfies the requirement until its expiry or review date.
When a person changes role or clinic, the module compares old and new learning rules.
Required new assignments are created with due dates.
No-longer-required assignments are closed with a clear reason rather than deleted.
rules: Exemptions are evidence based and time limited where appropriate.
Training completion and exemption remain distinguishable in reports.
Mandatory safety or legal learning may be configured as non-exemptible.

title: Accreditation, Quality & Regulatory Compliance
objective: Coordinate accreditation readiness, quality improvement, PDSA cycles, nursing and cold-chain duties, service feedback, audits and regulatory changes in one evidence-based workspace.
primaryUsers: Accreditation / Quality Lead, Practice Managers, Nursing Leads, Owners, Auditors
tabs: Accreditation Standards — Requirements, ownership, status and due dates.
Evidence Library — Evidence linked to standards, audits and reviews.
Gap Register — Unmet, partial or expiring requirements.
QI / PDSA — Improvement ideas, measures, cycles and outcomes.
Nursing & Cold Chain — Recurring clinical-operational duties and temperature exceptions.
Service Quality — Non-clinical feedback themes, waiting-time issues and recovery actions.
Regulatory Calendar — Known review dates, regulatory changes and implementation actions.
Audits — Internal audit plans, findings and follow-up.
visuals: Standards matrix showing Met, Partial, Not Met, Expiring and Not Applicable.
Evidence card with owner, version, review date and linked requirements.
PDSA board: Plan → Do → Study → Act with measures and decision.
Cold-chain chart and exception banner with escalation status.
Regulatory timeline with impact, affected modules, owner and readiness.
rules: Every accreditation requirement needs an owner, status, evidence position and review date.
Evidence may support multiple requirements but must retain its source and current version.
Gaps create owned actions and cannot be marked Met without reviewed evidence.
Temperature or clinical-operational exceptions follow defined escalation and incident rules.
QI cycles must record baseline, intended change, measure, result and decision.
Regulatory change actions link to policy, training, checklist and change-management activities as needed.

flows.title: Close an accreditation gap
steps: Lead opens Gap Register and selects a requirement.
The panel shows current status, missing evidence, owner and due date.
Lead creates or assigns gap actions and links relevant policy, checklist, training or ticket records.
When actions are complete, lead uploads/links evidence and submits for review.
Reviewer confirms the evidence and changes the requirement to Met or returns it with comments.

flows.title: Run a PDSA cycle
steps: User opens QI / PDSA and clicks Start PDSA.
Plan captures problem, baseline, proposed change, measure, owner and timeframe.
During Do, actions and observations are recorded.
Study compares results to baseline and captures learning.
In Act, the owner adopts, adapts or abandons the change and creates follow-up policy/training/checklist actions.

flows.title: Handle a cold-chain exception
steps: Nurse records a temperature reading in Nursing & Cold Chain.
An out-of-range value opens an exception modal requiring time, device, stock impact and immediate action.
The module prompts escalation, evidence and whether an incident/ticket is required.
Manager reviews and records disposition and corrective action.
The exception is included in compliance evidence and trend reporting.

flows.title: Process regulatory change
steps: Compliance owner adds a regulatory change with effective date and source summary.
Impact assessment identifies affected clinics, policies, training, checklists, communications and records.
Actions are assigned and tracked through Action Inbox.
Owner reviews evidence of implementation before the effective date.
The change is marked Implemented and scheduled for post-implementation review.

outputs: Measure: requirements Met with current evidence

title: Documents, Policies, SOPs & Intake
objective: Capture incoming documents and emails, maintain templates and location folders, control policies/SOPs and generated PDFs, and ensure every important document has an owner, status, version, review date and linked business purpose.
primaryUsers: Administration, Practice Managers, HR, Finance, Quality / Accreditation, Document Owners
tabs: Intake Queue — New emails, scans, invoices, certificates, forms and attachments awaiting classification.
Templates — Approved reusable forms, letters, checklists and document templates.
Location Folders — Clinic-specific controlled records and evidence.
Policies & SOPs — Approved business policies, procedures and work instructions.
Controlled Documents — Draft, review, approved, published, superseded and archived records.
Review Due — Upcoming and overdue reviews.
Acknowledgements — Required reading and acknowledgement status.
Search & Archive — Cross-folder search, filters and historical versions.
Retention & Legal Hold — Retention review, extension, controlled disposal and legal-hold protection.
visuals: Central intake queue with suggested category, sensitivity and owner.
Document metadata panel: title, type, clinic, owner, status, version, effective date, review date and links.
Side-by-side previous/current version comparison summary.
Review timeline and acknowledgement progress.
Template preview and PDF generation confirmation.
rules: No business-critical intake item should remain orphaned without classification, owner or filing decision.
Sensitive HR, finance, incident and credential documents inherit source-module permissions.
Approved documents are version-controlled; superseded versions remain accessible to authorised reviewers.
Published policies/SOPs require effective and review dates.
Required acknowledgements create learning/action records and cannot be inferred from email delivery.

flows.title: Process document intake
steps: Admin opens Intake Queue and selects an incoming item.
A classification drawer shows preview, suggested category, sensitivity and possible linked module.
Admin confirms category, clinic and owner, then chooses File, Create Action or Reject as Duplicate/Irrelevant.
If review is required, the item enters the owner’s Action Inbox.
After filing, the intake record shows destination and processing outcome.

flows.title: Publish a controlled policy
steps: Document owner opens Policies & SOPs and clicks Create New.
Owner starts from a template or uploads a draft, completes metadata and sets affected roles/clinics.
Owner submits for review; reviewers comment, approve or request changes.
On approval, owner clicks Publish and sets effective date and acknowledgement requirement.
Affected users receive acknowledgement tasks; the prior version becomes Superseded.

flows.title: Generate a controlled PDF
steps: User opens Templates and selects an approved template.
A guided form captures permitted business fields and linked record references.
User clicks Preview PDF and checks content, clinic branding and version.
User generates the PDF and chooses Store, Email through an approved workflow or Attach to Record.
The generated document is logged with template version and creator.

flows.title: Complete scheduled review
steps: Document owner opens Review Due and selects a record.
The review screen shows current version, usage links, incidents/gaps and prior review notes.
Owner chooses Confirm Current, Revise or Retire.
If revised, the document follows the approval and publication workflow.
The next review date is recorded and the review history remains visible.

flows.title: Document Retention, Legal Hold and Controlled Disposal
flows.objective: Manage end-of-retention decisions without keeping every document indefinitely or deleting records under hold.
flows.placement: Module 13 - Retention & Legal Hold.
steps: A document or record reaches its retention review date.
Owner reviews record category, business need, linked matters and any existing hold.
Owner selects Retain, Extend, Archive, Dispose or Place on Legal Hold.
Sensitive or bulk disposal is submitted for authorised approval.
Approved disposal follows the controlled method and records authority, date and evidence.
A legal hold prevents disposal, replacement or other action that would compromise the held record.
When the hold is released, the record returns to retention review rather than being immediately deleted.
rules: Legal hold overrides normal disposal scheduling.
Disposal is auditable and cannot be undone; approval must be proportionate to sensitivity.
Source-module permissions continue to apply.

flows.title: Workforce Data Access and Correction Request
flows.objective: Allow staff and doctors to request access to, or correction of, permitted business records about themselves.
flows.placement: Modules 3, 4 and 13, through a controlled self-service request.
steps: User opens self-service and submits an access or correction request.
The request identifies the record/category and explains the requested correction where applicable.
Authorised owner reviews identity, scope, sensitivity and any linked legal/retention restriction.
For access, permitted information is prepared and restricted third-party or sensitive information is excluded where appropriate.
For correction, the source owner approves, rejects or requests evidence.
Approved correction updates the source record through normal version/history rules.
The user receives the outcome, reason and completion date.
The request closes with a retained response history.
rules: Self-service access does not grant general HR, finance or incident permissions.
Corrections do not erase valid historical facts.
Response time and escalation follow approved privacy/business rules.
Priority 3 - Future Service Maturity

title: Ticketing Desk & Work Orders
objective: Centralise IT, facility, equipment, printer, operational and planned maintenance requests with priority, SLA, assignment, vendor involvement, evidence and manager sign-off.
primaryUsers: All Staff, Practice Managers, IT / Facilities, Asset Owners, Suppliers / Contractors where approved, Operations Managers
tabs: New Ticket — Guided issue reporting.
My Tickets — Tickets raised by or assigned to the user.
Team Queue — Clinic/team triage and assignment.
Work Orders — Approved work scope, contractor and completion details.
Planned Maintenance — Scheduled recurring maintenance and inspections.
SLA & Escalations — Priority targets, breaches and high-risk items.
Closed — Searchable closure history and evidence.
Duplicate & Linked Tickets — Detection, master-ticket selection, duplicate linking and shared updates.
Contractor Visits — Scheduled arrival, controlled site access, safety/privacy acknowledgement, check-out and work sign-off.
Reports — Volume, recurring issues, downtime and vendor performance.
visuals: Issue form with category, clinic, room, asset, impact, urgency, description and attachments.
Priority badge and SLA countdown.
Ticket timeline with assignments, updates, status changes and notifications.
Work-order panel for scope, supplier, cost approval, appointment and completion evidence.
Recurring issue banner linking related tickets and asset history.
rules: Priority is based on impact and urgency; P1/high-risk items trigger immediate escalation.
A ticket may link to clinic, room, asset, printer, website, checklist, incident or supplier.
Closure evidence is mandatory for defined categories and manager sign-off may be required.
Vendor access and sensitive information are limited to the approved scope.
Reopened tickets retain original closure details and reason for reopening.

flows.title: Report and resolve a standard issue
steps: Staff member clicks Report Issue or scans an asset QR code.
The form pre-fills clinic/asset where available; staff selects category, impact and description and adds evidence.
The ticket enters Team Queue where a manager confirms priority and assigns an owner.
Owner accepts, updates status and records work notes.
After completion, owner attaches evidence and clicks Mark Work Completed.
Manager reviews and clicks Close or returns the ticket for further work.

flows.title: Handle a P1 issue
steps: Reporter identifies a high-impact issue and submits the ticket.
The page displays P1 guidance and immediately notifies defined escalation contacts.
The assigned owner records containment and current service impact.
Updates remain visible in the escalation panel until service is restored.
Manager confirms resolution, root cause follow-up and whether an incident/RCA is required before closure.

flows.title: Create a vendor work order
steps: Manager opens a ticket and clicks Create Work Order.
The work-order form captures scope, supplier, access window, quote requirement, cost approval and safety/privacy conditions.
If a quote is required, the request enters finance/manager approval.
Approved work is scheduled and the vendor/owner records progress.
Completion evidence, invoice reference and manager sign-off close the work order and related ticket.

flows.title: Printer fault workflow
steps: User opens Printers in Inventory & Assets and clicks Raise Fault, or reports via QR.
Ticket receives printer location, model, serial, IP/queue and current toner/counter context.
Triage determines consumable, configuration, network or hardware issue and assigns internal support or supplier.
If unavailable, the fallback printer is displayed and staff are notified.
After repair, test-page evidence and service notes are added; counters/service history update on closure.

flows.title: Duplicate Ticket Detection and Ticket Merging
flows.objective: Prevent multiple users reporting the same outage or asset issue from fragmenting ownership and updates.
flows.placement: Module 14 - Duplicate & Linked Tickets.
steps: A reporter submits a ticket and the page displays possible existing matches.
Reporter may open the existing ticket or continue if the issue is different.
Triage user reviews related tickets and selects Merge as Duplicate where appropriate.
One ticket becomes the master operational record; duplicate tickets retain their original reporter and submission.
Duplicate reporters continue receiving authorised progress and closure updates.
SLA, assignment, work order and root-cause follow-up are managed from the master ticket.
Closing the master ticket updates linked duplicates while preserving each history.
rules: Merging does not delete the original report.
Tickets from different confidentiality levels are not merged inappropriately.
A duplicate can be separated again only with a reason.

flows.title: Contractor Arrival, Site Access and Work Completion
flows.objective: Control third-party attendance at clinics and connect access, safety and completion evidence to the work order.
flows.placement: Module 14 - Contractor Visits, linked to Module 15 suppliers/assets.
steps: Approved work order schedules the contractor visit and nominates a site contact.
On arrival, the contractor or site contact opens Check In Contractor.
Identity, supplier, work order and permitted areas are confirmed.
Required safety, privacy and access conditions are acknowledged.
Work progress and any change in scope are recorded.
At completion, evidence, test results, parts used and outstanding work are recorded.
Site contact checks the area/asset and completes contractor check-out.
Manager signs off the work order or returns it for further work.
rules: Contractor access is limited to approved time, scope and areas.
Scope/cost changes require approval before work continues where defined.
No contractor receives general platform access by default.

flows.title: In-Product Help, Support and Feedback
flows.objective: Help users complete work correctly and report problems without losing page or record context.
flows.placement: Global help experience linked to Module 14 Ticketing Desk.
steps: User opens Help from any page.
The panel displays guidance relevant to the user's role and current workflow.
User searches or opens the recommended instruction.
If unresolved, user clicks Report a Problem.
The support form carries current page/module/record context and allows description and attachment.
The resulting ticket appears in My Support Requests.
User receives updates and may confirm resolution or provide feedback.
rules: Help content is business-facing and version controlled.
Sensitive record content is not copied into support unnecessarily.
Support requests follow normal ticket priority and permission rules.

flows.title: Customer Support Escalation and Service-Impact Communication
flows.objective: Provide a mature support journey for future external clinic customers.
flows.placement: Module 20 - Customer Support Escalations, linked to Module 14.
steps: Customer raises a support request and selects the affected area and impact.
Support triages severity and assigns an owner and target.
Where investigation requires tenant data, support requests time-limited access with reason and scope.
Customer/authorised owner approves, rejects or limits access.
Support provides progress updates and workarounds.
If multiple tenants are affected, an approved service-impact communication is issued without exposing other customers.
Resolution is confirmed with the customer and temporary access expires.
For significant events, a post-incident summary and prevention actions are recorded.
rules: Support access is never assumed.
Cross-customer communications contain no tenant-specific confidential information.
Customer closure feedback does not remove internal follow-up actions.

title: Inventory, Suppliers, Finance & Assets
objective: Manage stock levels, transfers, supplier invoice review, supplier/contract governance, non-patient finance approvals, clinic assets, biomedical equipment and printer fleet lifecycle without duplicating patient billing.
primaryUsers: Practice Managers, Inventory Owners, Finance Users, Asset / IT / Facilities Owners, Owners
tabs: Inventory — Item register, PAR levels, quantities and clinic ownership.
Low Stock & Orders — Reorder queue, purchase requests and order status.
Transfers & Adjustments — Inter-clinic stock movement, wastage and corrections.
Invoice OCR — Supplier invoice upload, extracted fields, review and approval.
Suppliers & Contracts — Supplier ownership, contacts, terms, reviews and performance.
Finance Approvals — Operational invoice thresholds, duplicates and anomalies.
Assets & Equipment — Asset register, ownership, warranty and status.
Printers — Fleet details, toner, counters, network/queue and fallback.
Service Calendar — Service, calibration, warranty and planned maintenance.
Replacement Plan — Risk, age, cost and approval for replacement/retirement.
Stocktake — Full and cycle counts by clinic, room or item category with controlled variance approval.
Expiry & Recall — Batch/location tracking, quarantine, return, write-off and recall completion evidence.
Asset Assignment & Loans — Issue, transfer, temporary loan, return, loss and decommissioning.
Supplier Onboarding — Supplier due diligence, approved categories, quote comparison, activation and suspension.
visuals: Stock cards with on-hand, PAR, reorder, clinic and criticality.
OCR split view showing invoice image and editable extracted fields with confidence flags.
Duplicate and price-change warning panel.
Asset profile with QR, location/room, owner, warranty, service and linked tickets.

Printer profile fields: clinic, room, brand/model, serial/asset ID, hostname, IP address, network segment, connection path, print queue, driver, toner levels, counters, fallback printer, supplier/support and service due date.
rules: Stock adjustments, transfers, write-offs and invoice approvals require reason and history.
OCR results do not update stock or finance records until reviewed and approved.
Duplicate invoice number, repeated total and unusual price movement are flagged for review.
Critical assets require owner, service/calibration rule and escalation for overdue service.
Printer records must support operational fallback and linked work-order history.
Supplier and contract reviews create actions before expiry or renewal dates.

flows.title: Low-stock reorder
steps: Inventory owner opens Low Stock & Orders and reviews items below PAR.
User selects items and clicks Create Purchase Request.
The request groups items by supplier and clinic and shows expected quantity/cost.
Authorised manager approves or adjusts the request.
On delivery, user clicks Receive Stock, records quantities and discrepancies, and updates on-hand balance.

flows.title: Supplier invoice OCR
steps: Finance/inventory user opens Invoice OCR and uploads an invoice.
The split view displays extracted supplier, invoice number/date, GST, total and line items with confidence flags.
User corrects fields and links items, order and clinic.
Duplicate and price-change warnings are reviewed and resolved.
User submits for approval; after approval, invoice register and permitted stock receipts update.
The original invoice and approved extract remain linked.

flows.title: Inter-clinic stock transfer
steps: User opens Transfers & Adjustments and clicks Transfer Stock.
The form captures source clinic, destination clinic, items, quantities, reason and responsible staff.
Source owner dispatches and destination owner receives.
Any discrepancy requires reason and manager review.
Both clinic balances and the movement history update after receipt confirmation.

flows.title: Add and service an asset
steps: Asset owner opens Assets & Equipment and clicks Add Asset.
The wizard captures category, criticality, clinic/room, owner, serial, warranty, supplier and service/calibration schedule.
A QR label is generated and the asset becomes Active.
Before service due date, an action appears in Service Calendar.
Service completion records provider, date, outcome, evidence and next due date.

flows.title: Add and manage a printer
steps: IT/asset user opens Printers and clicks Add Printer.
The form captures physical, asset, network, queue, driver, toner, counter, supplier, support and fallback details.
User saves and performs a readiness review; incomplete operational fields remain amber.
Toner and service due alerts appear in the module and Action Inbox.
A fault can be raised directly from the printer profile and follows the work-order flow.

flows.title: Supplier contract review
steps: Contract owner opens Suppliers & Contracts and selects a contract due for review.
The review screen shows spend, tickets, SLA, price changes, incidents and expiry terms.
