Owner records Renew, Renegotiate, Replace or End recommendation.
Required approval and follow-up actions are assigned.
The outcome, new dates and documents are stored in contract history.

flows.title: Stocktake, Expiry, Batch Recall and Product Return
flows.objective: Complete inventory assurance beyond ordering and transfers by controlling counts, variances, expiry and recall disposition.
flows.placement: Module 15 - Stocktake and Expiry & Recall tabs.
steps: Manager creates a full or cycle stocktake and assigns count areas.
Staff count items and submit quantities and notes.
The platform compares counted and recorded quantities and creates variance review items.
Authorised manager approves adjustments and the stock balance updates with history.
For expiry or recall, the owner selects the affected item/batch and locates quantities by clinic and room.
Affected stock is quarantined and made unavailable for normal use.
The owner records return to supplier, transfer, write-off or other approved disposition.
Completion evidence and unresolved quantities are reviewed before the recall/expiry action is closed.
rules: Stock balance changes require approved variance or movement records.
Quarantined stock is visibly unavailable.
Recall closure requires all known locations to be resolved or explicitly escalated.
Priority 2 - Strong Governance

flows.title: Supplier Onboarding, Quote Comparison and Supplier Suspension
flows.objective: Ensure suppliers are approved, appropriately evidenced and monitored before use.
flows.placement: Module 15 - Suppliers & Contracts and Supplier Onboarding.
steps: Owner clicks Onboard Supplier and completes identity, contacts, service categories, evidence and terms.
Required due-diligence items are assigned for review.
Where procurement comparison is required, quotes are entered and compared against the same scope.
Approver records the selected supplier and rationale.
Approved supplier becomes selectable for permitted work and orders.
Expired evidence, serious performance issues or incidents trigger a restriction/suspension review.
Authorised manager suspends, reinstates or ends the supplier and open work is reassigned where necessary.
rules: Unapproved or suspended suppliers cannot be selected for new work without authorised exception.
Quote comparisons retain non-price considerations.
Supplier status changes are effective-dated and auditable.

flows.title: Asset Assignment, Loan, Loss, Return and Decommissioning
flows.objective: Track responsibility for portable or sensitive assets throughout issue, transfer, return and retirement.
flows.placement: Module 15 - Asset Assignment & Loans.
steps: Asset owner selects an active asset and clicks Assign / Loan Asset.
Holder, clinic, issue date, expected return date and condition are recorded.
Recipient acknowledges receipt and any use conditions.
Transfers and extensions are recorded as new movement events.
On return, the asset is inspected and condition/evidence are recorded.
If lost or stolen, the user records the event and links an incident, access review or replacement action.
For retirement, owner confirms data/access removal, disposal method, approval and final status.
rules: An asset has one accountable holder/location at a time.
Sensitive devices require access/data-removal confirmation before disposal.
History remains visible after retirement.

outputs: Supplier invoice and OCR extract register

title: Incidents, Complaints, Risk & Continuity
objective: Capture operational and non-clinical incidents, complaints, risks, privacy/cyber events and downtime; support triage, investigation, RCA/CAPA, business continuity and evidence-based closure.
primaryUsers: All Staff as reporters, Practice Managers, Operations / Risk, Privacy / Security Owners, Owners, Quality Leads
tabs: Report — Guided incident, complaint or risk submission.
Active Incidents — Triage, severity, ownership and current status.
Complaints — Service complaint handling and response actions.
Risk Register — Identified risks, controls, ratings and reviews.
Investigations — Evidence, interviews, chronology and findings.
RCA / CAPA — Root cause, corrective and preventive actions.
Business Continuity — Plans, contacts, critical services and exercises.
Downtime Events — Activation, impact, recovery and review.
Privacy / Cyber — Suspected breach, containment, assessment and actions.
Lessons & Trends — Themes, recurrence and linked improvement work.
Near Miss & Confidential Reporting — Near-miss capture and approved confidential/anonymous reporting pathways.
Continuity Exercises — Scenario-based tests for power, internet, phone, practice-system, building, weather, staffing and cyber disruption.
visuals: Confidential report wizard with clear urgency guidance.
Severity and escalation banner with responsible owner and due dates.
Investigation timeline and evidence list.
RCA cause tree / contributing factor form and CAPA tracker.
Business continuity event board showing affected services, workaround, communications and recovery status.
rules: High-risk events trigger immediate escalation according to approved business rules.
Sensitive reports are restricted by role and clinic.
Closure requires outcome, evidence, action status and approval where defined.
Corrective/preventive actions link to Tasks, Training, Policies, Checklists, Tickets or Change Management.
Privacy/cyber events require controlled access, containment record and responsible-owner review.
Reopening requires reason and retains the original closure decision.

flows.title: Report and investigate an incident
steps: Reporter clicks Report Incident and selects category, clinic, date/time, immediate risk and description.
Urgent guidance appears; reporter records immediate action and submits.
Triage owner reviews severity, confidentiality and required escalation.
Investigator builds chronology, adds evidence and records contributing factors.
RCA/CAPA actions are created and assigned.
When actions and evidence meet closure criteria, investigator submits closure and authorised manager approves.

flows.title: Manage a complaint
steps: Manager logs or receives a complaint through the controlled intake path.
The complaint record captures service theme, preferred contact pathway, acknowledgement due and owner without unnecessary clinical detail.
Owner investigates, records communication and creates service recovery actions.
If risk or serious event is identified, the record links to an incident.
Manager approves response and closure; themes feed Service Quality reporting.

flows.title: Activate downtime plan
steps: Authorised user opens Business Continuity and clicks Activate Plan.
The event form captures affected clinic/service, start time, impact and decision owner.
The event board displays critical contacts, approved workaround checklists and communications.
Teams update status until recovery is confirmed.
Owner records recovery time, outstanding actions and post-event review; lessons create follow-up actions.

flows.title: Privacy/cyber response
steps: User logs a suspected privacy/cyber event with minimal necessary detail.
The restricted workflow prompts immediate containment and responsible-owner notification.
Owner assesses scope, affected systems/records, evidence and required advice/notification decisions.
Corrective actions, access reviews, communication and training tasks are assigned.
Closure requires documented assessment, actions and review approval.

flows.title: Anonymous or Near-Miss Reporting and Complaint Review
flows.objective: Encourage early reporting while protecting confidentiality and providing a review path for unresolved complaints.
flows.placement: Module 16 - Near Miss & Confidential Reporting and Complaints.
steps: Reporter selects Report Near Miss or confidential reporting pathway and records minimum necessary facts.
The report enters restricted triage with identity visibility limited according to the chosen pathway and approved rules.
Triage owner assesses severity, immediate controls and whether investigation is required.
Near misses may create prevention actions without being treated as completed harm events.
For complaints, the owner records acknowledgement, investigation, response and service-recovery actions.
If the complainant remains dissatisfied, an authorised review or escalation is opened.
External regulator, insurer, legal or other referral decisions are recorded where applicable.
Final outcome and lessons feed trends without exposing unnecessary identity.
rules: Anonymous reporting limitations are explained clearly.
Confidentiality is not promised beyond approved business/legal limits.
Complaint escalation does not overwrite the original response.

flows.title: Scenario-Based Business Continuity and Exercise
flows.objective: Provide usable playbooks for common clinic disruptions and confirm recovery through exercises and real events.
flows.placement: Module 16 - Business Continuity and Continuity Exercises.
steps: Authorised user selects a scenario and chooses Live Event or Exercise.
The plan records affected clinic/services, start time, decision owner and current impact.
Roles, contacts and approved workaround checklists are assigned.
Internal/external operational communications are issued as required.
Teams update service status, risks and workaround progress.
When service is restored, the owner confirms recovery and identifies any backlog created during downtime.
Backlog reconciliation and outstanding actions are completed.
A post-event or exercise review records lessons, plan changes, training and follow-up actions.
rules: Exercise notifications cannot be mistaken for a live incident.
Workarounds do not create duplicate patient records in this platform.
Recovery is not complete until critical backlog and open risks are addressed.

outputs: Business continuity event and exercise report
Measure: high-risk events triaged within target

title: Email & SMS Communications
objective: Plan, approve, send and monitor operational and marketing email/SMS communications using approved templates, audience controls, consent/suppression rules and delivery reporting.
primaryUsers: Authorised Marketing / Communications, Practice Managers, Owners / Approvers, Administration
tabs: Email Campaigns — Draft, approval, scheduled, sent and completed email campaigns.
SMS Campaigns — Operational and approved marketing SMS.
Templates — Approved content, branding and mandatory wording.
Audience — Approved lists, filters, exclusions and source reference.
Approvals — Campaign decision queue and version review.
Delivery — Sent, delivered, failed, bounced and retry status.
Conversations — Permitted two-way messages where enabled.
Consent & Suppression — Opt-out, do-not-contact and excluded recipients.
Reports — Campaign performance, delivery and compliance.
Emergency Communications — Approved urgent templates, rapid approval, linked updates, all-clear and failure escalation.
visuals: Campaign builder stepper: Purpose → Audience → Content → Review → Approval → Schedule.
Desktop/mobile email preview and SMS character/segment indicator.
Audience summary showing source, included, excluded, duplicates and consent suppression.
Approval comparison showing changes since prior version.
Delivery dashboard with failure reason and retry action.
rules: Only approved templates and authorised users can send campaigns.
Audience counts must exclude suppressed, invalid and duplicate recipients before approval.
Campaign approval is tied to the exact content and audience version.
Opt-out and communication preferences are respected in all future sends.
Sensitive clinical or payment information must not be sent through general campaigns.
Failed delivery creates a review/retry action without duplicating successful sends.

flows.title: Create and send a campaign
steps: User clicks Create Email Campaign or Create SMS Campaign.
The stepper captures purpose, clinic/brand, approved audience source and exclusions.
User selects a template, edits permitted content and previews the message.
User sends a test and resolves validation warnings.
User submits for approval; approver reviews exact content, audience count and schedule.
After approval, the campaign is scheduled or sent and delivery appears in the dashboard.

flows.title: Handle failed deliveries
steps: User opens Delivery and filters to Failed.
The page groups failures by invalid address/number, temporary failure, suppression or gateway issue.
User selects eligible temporary failures and clicks Retry Failed.
Permanent failures are marked for source-data correction and do not retry automatically.
The campaign report shows original and retry outcomes without double-counting.

flows.title: Update suppression
steps: Authorised user opens Consent & Suppression and searches the contact reference.
User records the approved preference or opt-out source and effective date.
The interface confirms which channels are suppressed.
Future campaign audience previews automatically exclude the suppressed contact.
Any authorised reversal requires reason and evidence.

flows.title: Emergency Communication and Campaign Cancellation
flows.objective: Support urgent operational messages and safely control already scheduled or in-progress communications.
flows.placement: Module 17 - Emergency Communications and Campaigns.
steps: Authorised user selects an approved emergency template and links the relevant incident, outage or clinic transition.
Audience, clinic scope, exclusions and communication channel are confirmed.
Urgent approval is completed according to severity rules.
Message is sent and delivery failures are prioritised for review.
Further updates and the all-clear remain linked to the original communication event.
For a scheduled normal campaign, user may cancel before sending and records a reason.
If content or audience changes after approval, the approval expires and the revised version must be reviewed again.
If a send can be paused, successful recipients are not sent duplicates when activity resumes.
rules: Emergency messages remain operational and avoid sensitive clinical detail.
Cancellation does not recall messages already delivered.
All related messages share one event history.

title: Digital Operations & Security
objective: Monitor clinic websites and digital services, control remote-support access, govern password/secret ownership and rotation, manage security-camera access requests and review device/connector health.
primaryUsers: IT / Security, Owners, Operations Managers, Approved Support Users, Auditors
tabs: Website Monitoring — Availability, response time, outages and recovery.
SSL / Domain — Expiry, ownership and renewal actions.
Remote Access — Approved endpoints, requests, sessions and emergency access.
Password / Secrets — Credential ownership, access requests, rotation and review.
Security Cameras — Camera inventory, health, viewing and footage requests.
Device / Connector Health — Operational status and assigned owner.
Access Reviews — Periodic review of sensitive digital access.
Reports — Outage, access, rotation and health history.
visuals: Website health cards with current state, response time, recent outages and SSL days remaining.
Remote endpoint register with clinic, asset, tool, sensitivity and owner.
Access request drawer showing purpose, duration and approver.
Credential governance card with owner, rotation due and last review; plain-text display is avoided where governance-only.
Camera map/list with zone, purpose, privacy classification, health and request history.
rules: A single transient website failure should follow the configured threshold before major outage escalation.
Sensitive remote access requires approved purpose and is logged by user, time, asset and clinic.
Emergency/break-glass access triggers immediate notification and after-the-fact review.
Credential reveal/copy/export requires reason and is auditable; high-risk credentials may require approval.
Camera access is limited by role, clinic, zone and approved purpose; export requires approval and reason.
Camera zones, signage, audio status and retention rules require business/privacy approval before use.

flows.title: Website outage response
steps: Monitoring identifies repeated failures and creates an outage alert.
IT user opens Website Monitoring and reviews status, response history and affected site.
User acknowledges the alert and creates a ticket/incident if required.
Updates and recovery time are recorded.
After recovery, the outage closes and monthly uptime reporting updates.

flows.title: Remote access request
steps: Support user opens Remote Access and selects an endpoint.
User clicks Request Access and enters purpose, expected duration and related ticket.
Approver reviews sensitivity and scope and approves, rejects or limits duration.
User launches the approved session; start/end and reason are logged.
The session closes and any emergency or unusual access enters review.

flows.title: High-risk secret access
steps: User opens Password / Secrets and requests access to a restricted record.
The request shows owner, sensitivity, reason and linked ticket/change.
Approver grants time-limited reveal/copy permission or rejects.
User performs the allowed action; the event is logged.
If rotation is required after use, a rotation task is created and tracked.

flows.title: Camera footage request
steps: Authorised user opens Security Cameras and clicks Request Footage.
The form captures camera/zone, date/time range, purpose and intended use/export.
Approver reviews privacy, scope and authority.
Approved viewing/export is performed through the controlled source and logged.
The request closes with outcome, evidence reference and retention instruction.

outputs: Remote access register and emergency review
Camera inventory, health and footage request report

title: Clinic Analytics, Data Quality & Change
objective: Provide aggregate clinic flow and capacity insight, deeper benchmarking, master-data hygiene, change impact management and release/readiness control without creating patient-level operational workflows.
primaryUsers: Owners, Operations Managers, Practice Managers, Data Owners, Change / Training / Compliance Owners
tabs: Capacity & Flow — Aggregate provider availability, demand, waiting and utilisation trends.
Operational Trends — Roster, attendance, tasks, tickets, stock and quality trends.
Benchmark Detail — Comparable clinic metrics and contributing factors.
Data Quality — Missing, duplicate, expired, inconsistent and stale records.
Change Register — Proposed, assessed, approved, implemented and reviewed changes.
Impact Assessment — People, process, compliance, communication, finance and training impacts.
Readiness — Actions required before an effective date or business release.
Improvement Backlog — Prioritised improvement ideas and benefits.
Rollback & Benefits Review — Pause, rollback, correct-forward and expected-versus-actual benefit assessment.
visuals: Aggregate capacity charts by clinic, day and provider group with no patient identifiers.
Benchmark cards with definition, threshold and drill-down.
Data quality dashboard with completeness score and owner.
Change impact checklist and dependency map linking policies, training, checklists and communications.
Readiness status showing Not Started, At Risk, Ready and Implemented.
rules: Analytics must clearly label data period, definition, exclusions and refresh status.
Data quality exceptions require an owner; critical incomplete data can block roster/pay/compliance workflows.
Duplicates are resolved without deleting required history.
Meaningful business changes require reason, owner, impact, effective date, communication/training decision and post-change review.
Policy, pay rule, template and critical workflow changes are versioned and effective-dated.

flows.title: Review clinic capacity
steps: Manager opens Capacity & Flow and selects clinic and period.
Aggregate charts show demand, provider availability, waiting indicators and utilisation.
Manager selects an outlier and opens contributing summary, not patient records.
Manager clicks Create Action to address roster, opening hours, provider coverage or process issue.
The action is assigned and tracked through Action Inbox and later trend review.

flows.title: Correct data-quality issue
steps: Data owner opens Data Quality and filters to Critical.
The page shows missing/duplicate/stale record, affected workflows and assigned owner.
Owner opens the source record and corrects or submits a merge/review decision.
Reviewer confirms the correction where sensitive or high-impact.
The next quality check clears the exception and updates the clinic data-health score.

flows.title: Manage a business change
steps: Owner clicks Raise Change and records reason, desired outcome, affected clinics and effective date.
Impact Assessment prompts review of staff, policies, training, checklists, communications, privacy, finance and downtime.
Required actions and approvers are assigned.
When readiness items are complete, approver confirms Go Live / Effective.
After implementation, owner starts Post-Change Review and records outcomes, incidents and further actions.

flows.title: Failed Change, Rollback and Benefit-Realisation Review
flows.objective: Provide a controlled response when an approved business change causes problems or does not achieve the intended outcome.
flows.placement: Module 19 - Change Register, Rollback & Benefits Review.
steps: After implementation, the change owner records actual performance and any incidents, complaints or gaps.
If the change is unsafe or unsuccessful, the owner selects Pause, Rollback or Correct Forward.
The impact panel identifies affected clinics, users, policies, training, communications and records.
Required approval is obtained and affected users are notified.
Rollback/correction actions are executed and linked incidents/tickets are monitored.
The owner confirms stabilisation and records any permanent revisions.
At the scheduled benefits review, expected and actual outcomes, cost, risk and lessons are compared.
Further improvement actions are created or the change is formally closed.
rules: Rollback decisions are as auditable as original approvals.
A failed change is not marked successful merely because tasks were completed.
Measures and review dates are defined before go-live wherever possible.

outputs: Aggregate clinic capacity and flow report
Data quality dashboard and exception register
Measure: changes implemented with readiness complete

title: Commercial SaaS & Future Workspaces
objective: Prepare a future commercial version for onboarding external clinic groups, controlling subscribed modules, support access, branding, usage, renewals, offboarding and optional department workspaces.
primaryUsers: Owner / Commercial Manager, SaaS Administrator, Customer Success / Support, Finance / Billing, Tenant Administrator
tabs: Tenants — Customer clinic groups, status, contacts and contract dates.
Plans & Modules — Subscribed capability packages and limits.
Onboarding — Customer configuration, training and acceptance checklist.
Branding & Settings — Approved tenant-level business preferences.
Support Access — Time-limited support requests, reasons and review.
Usage & Adoption — Module use, active users and configuration gaps.
Renewals — Renewal dates, risks, decisions and actions.
Offboarding — Export, retention, access removal and closure checklist.
Future Departments — Optional controlled workspaces with tasks and documents.
Subscription & Billing — Trial conversion, plan changes, billing contacts, failed payment, suspension and reinstatement.
Customer Support Escalations — Severity, temporary access, progress updates, service-impact communications and post-incident summary.
visuals: Tenant health cards with onboarding, adoption, support, renewal and risk status.
Module entitlement checklist and business configuration preview.
Onboarding stepper with owners, due dates and acceptance evidence.
Support-access banner showing who, why and expiry.
Offboarding checklist covering access, open work, records, exports and confirmation.
rules: Customer/tenant settings and records are separated in the user experience; support access is never assumed.
Support users require a ticket/reason and time-limited approval to view customer records.
Module packaging and plan limits are explicit to tenant administrators.
Offboarding follows an approved retention/export/access-removal checklist.
Optional department workspaces remain controlled and are not added to the main navigation unless activated.

flows.title: Onboard a tenant
steps: Commercial admin opens Tenants and clicks Add Tenant.
The wizard captures customer identity, contacts, plan, modules, contract dates and support owner.
Tenant admin is invited and completes clinic, user and business-setting information.
Onboarding checklist covers configuration, training, sample workflows and acceptance.
Commercial admin completes Configuration Review and activates the tenant.

flows.title: Grant support access
steps: Support user opens Support Access and selects the tenant and related support ticket.
The request captures purpose, modules, duration and required data scope.
Tenant or authorised owner approves, rejects or limits the request.
A visible banner remains during the support-access period.
Access expires automatically according to the approved business duration and enters review history.

flows.title: Manage renewal
steps: Commercial manager opens Renewals and selects a tenant approaching renewal.
The screen shows adoption, open issues, plan, modules, support history and contract date.
Manager records renewal recommendation and creates customer actions.
Approved changes to modules/plan are scheduled for the renewal date.
Renewal outcome and next review date are stored.

flows.title: Offboard tenant
steps: Authorised admin clicks Start Offboarding.
Checklist identifies open actions, support access, users, reports, documents and agreed export/retention steps.
Tenant admin confirms required exports and closure date.
Access is suspended, outstanding responsibilities are completed and closure is reviewed.
Tenant is archived with a formal offboarding record.

flows.title: Commercial Plan Upgrade, Downgrade and Subscription Billing
flows.objective: Complete the future SaaS commercial lifecycle beyond onboarding and renewal.
flows.placement: Module 20 - Subscription & Billing.
steps: Tenant administrator or commercial manager opens the current plan and selects Upgrade, Downgrade or Change Modules.
The page shows entitlement, limits, price/effective-date summary and operational impact.
Required customer and internal approvals are completed.
Upgrade changes activate on the approved date; downgrade identifies records/actions requiring completion or export first.
Billing-contact changes are confirmed and recorded.
A failed subscription payment creates a commercial action and approved customer communication.
If unresolved, tenant access may be restricted according to contract while essential offboarding/export options remain available.
On resolution, authorised user reinstates the tenant and records the outcome.
rules: Plan changes do not remove historical records.
Suspension and reinstatement follow contract and approval rules.
Commercial billing remains separate from clinic patient billing.

flows.title: Customer Support Escalation and Service-Impact Communication
flows.objective: Provide a mature support journey for future external clinic customers.
flows.placement: Module 20 - Customer Support Escalations, linked to Module 14.
steps: Customer raises a support request and selects the affected area and impact.
Support triages severity and assigns an owner and target.
Where investigation requires tenant data, support requests time-limited access with reason and scope.
Customer/authorised owner approves, rejects or limits access.
Support provides progress updates and workarounds.
If multiple tenants are affected, an approved service-impact communication is issued without exposing other customers.
Resolution is confirmed with the customer and temporary access expires.
For significant events, a post-incident summary and prevention actions are recorded.
rules: Support access is never assumed.
Cross-customer communications contain no tenant-specific confidential information.
Customer closure feedback does not remove internal follow-up actions.

outputs: Measure: tenants activated without critical setup gaps
Measure: support access events with valid approval
Expanded User Flows and Lifecycle Scenarios

Version 2.0 adds the following normal, exception and lifecycle journeys to the existing twenty-module structure. These are not new sidebar modules unless explicitly stated; they are tabs, workspaces or linked flows inside the existing modules.
